title: Argentina star hit with one of the biggest bans in World Cup history
byline: FIFA banned three Argentina players overnight, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents after losing the World Cup final.

title: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga wins Lausanne Diamond League
byline: Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage produced a stunning performance at the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland, securing victory in the men’s javelin throw with an impressive effort of 88.14 metres.

title: World’s oldest living person celebrates 117th birthday
byline: The world’s oldest living person turns 117 on Friday.

title: President pays final respects to veteran singer Nanda Malini
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake paid his final respects to legendary Sri Lankan singer Visharad Dr. Nanda Malini, who passed away on August 20 at the age of 82.

title: Nine deaths reported due to adverse weather conditions
byline: Nine deaths have been reported in several districts due to adverse weather conditions across the country, according to the Disaster Management Centre (DMC).

title: Showers possible after 2 p.m. in Eastern districts
byline: Showers may occur at a few places in the Ampara, Monaragala and Batticaloa districts after 2 p.m. today, while mainly dry weather is expected to prevail in other parts of the island, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Tesla and others begin record vehicle recall in China
byline: Tesla and eight other automakers said on Friday they will recall a total of about 4.3 million vehicles ​in China over concerns that doors may be difficult to open in an emergency, marking the country’s largest automotive recall.

title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
byline: TikTok has agreed to pay $400m (£293m) to the US to end a lawsuit alleging its platform violated children‘s privacy, marking one of the largest ever settlements over the issue.

title: Govt to strengthen specialist healthcare services: Health Minister
byline: The Health and Mass Media Ministry is committed to strengthening specialist healthcare services, improving postgraduate medical education, expanding hospital infrastructure and introducing modern medical technology to address future challenges in the health sector, Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: Sri Lanka’s fish harvest in steady decline since 2014
byline: Sri Lanka’s fish harvest has been steadily declining since 2014, raising concerns over the long-term sustainability of the country’s marine resources, the National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Institute (NARA) says.

title: Paredes receives 10-game suspension, three Argentina players punished by FIFA following World Cup final fallout
byline: Argentina’s Leandro Paredes has been handed a ten‑match suspension by FIFA for his role in a post‑match brawl following the 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey.

title: Jaffna temple festival eye injuries raise concerns over possible UV exposure
byline: Symptoms reported by 157 people including 58 men, 44 women and 55 children treated at Jaffna Teaching Hospital after attending a Hindu temple festival have raised serious concerns over possible ultraviolet (UV) eye injuries, a senior eye doctor said.

title: US-Canada trade war reignites as talks fail at last minute
byline: Trade talks between Canada and the United States failed at the last minute on Friday night, reigniting the North American trade war, with Ottawa vowing to match Washington’s tariffs.

title: World’s oldest living person celebrates 117th birthday
byline: The world’s oldest living person turns 117 on Friday.

title: Cancer drug reportedly sold for over Rs. 25,000 amid shortage
byline: An essential medicine used to protect cancer patients from infections is reportedly being sold for more than Rs. 25,000 on the black market amid a severe shortage in the country, the Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights said.

title: Tesla and others begin record vehicle recall in China
byline: Tesla and eight other automakers said on Friday they will recall a total of about 4.3 million vehicles ​in China over concerns that doors may be difficult to open in an emergency, marking the country’s largest automotive recall.

title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
byline: TikTok has agreed to pay $400m (£293m) to the US to end a lawsuit alleging its platform violated children‘s privacy, marking one of the largest ever settlements over the issue.

title: Fire at Anawilundawa Ramsar Wetland brought under control; Probe underway
byline: A sudden fire that broke out at the Anawilundawa Ramsar Wetland Sanctuary has been brought fully under control, with the damage limited to approximately eight acres, the Ministry of Environment said.

title: Final Kumbal Perahera to take to Kandy streets today
byline: The final Kumbal Perahera of the historic Kandy Esala Perahera will take to the streets of Kandy today (22), marking another major highlight of the annual religious and cultural festival.

title: Sri Lankan Podcasters convene for landmark media landscape forum in Colombo
byline: The Podcasters’ Association of Sri Lanka recently hosted a high-level discussion titled ’’Exploring the New Media Landscape’’ at the Granbell Hotel in Colombo. Bringing together over 100 digital content creators, media professionals, and industry stakeholders, the event focused on the central theme of navigating structural challenges, identifying new opportunities, and fostering sustainable growth for the nation’s creator economy.

title: Miss Teen Sri Lanka leaves for India
byline: Miss Teen Sri Lanka 2026, Divyangana Seneviratne, left the country from Bandaranaike International Airport today (22) to represent Sri Lanka at the Miss Teen International 2026 beauty pageant in Jaipur, India.

title: Govt committed to equal rights and opportunities for all: PM
byline: Ensuring equal rights and equal opportunities for all citizens, without leaving anyone behind, is a fundamental policy of the Government, Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya said.

title: Namal urges President to act on allegations involving Presidential Secretary
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has called on President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to take appropriate action over allegations concerning the Presidential Secretary, saying such action would demonstrate the Government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.

title: Major reservoirs hold 35.9% of effective storage capacity
byline: The total effective water storage of the countr’s major reservoirs stood at 35.9% as of August 21, according to the latest data from the Irrigation Department’s Water Management Branch.

title: Father leaves 7-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji to continue hike, reports say
byline: A father has been reprimanded by police after leaving his son on Japan’s highest mountain for several hours with just a soft drink and snack, local media report.

title: ‘Bus Lalith’ to be brought back from Dubai
byline: Organized criminal and drug trafficker Lalith Kannangara, alias “Bus Lalith Anidda” (24), who was arrested in Dubai, is scheduled to be brought back to Sri Lanka tomorrow, police said.

title: Police clearance online system restored
byline: The digital data system used to process police clearance certificates has been restored and applications can now be submitted through the usual online procedure, the Sri Lanka Police said

title: Laptop catches fire on US flight, with passenger treated at airport
byline: One person has received medical treatment after a passenger’s laptop caught fire on an American Airlines flight.

title: Heat index alert issued for several areas
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a heat index alert for the Eastern and North Central provinces and several districts in the North and Uva provinces, warning that the temperature felt by the human body could reach the ‘Caution’ level in some areas during the daytime.

title: One should not monkey with the Judiciary: Eminent lawyer
byline: Highlighting that the present government will one day understand why there is so much opposition to the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, past President of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) Saliya Peiris stressed that ’one must not monkey with the Judiciary’.

title: Sugeeshwara Bandara admitted to prison hospital
byline: Sugeeshwara Bandara, former private secretary to ex-President Gotabaya Rajapaksa, has been admitted to the prison hospital after a wound on his leg reportedly worsened.

title: Sri Lanka to strengthen management of shark fishing industry
byline: The Fisheries, Aquatic and Marine Resources Ministry has initiated a programme to strengthen the management of Sri Lanka’s shark fishing industry in line with international standards.

title: Two-time world champion Tete shot dead outside home
byline: Two-time world champion Zolani Tete has been shot dead outside his home in South Africa.

title: 81,000 affected as dry spell deepens
byline: More than 81,000 people across seven districts are facing the effects of the prevailing dry weather, with growing concerns over access to drinking water, the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) said.

title: Polonnaruwa records highest temperature at 37.2°C
byline: Polonnaruwa recorded the highest temperature in Sri Lanka at 37.2°C today (22), according to temperature data released by the Department of Meteorology.
